mechanisms.name: Is it true?
mechanisms.paraphrase: Every belief and every one of the principles themselves is to be tested with the question 'Is it true?' rather than adopted on authority.

mechanisms.name: Truth as foundation
mechanisms.paraphrase: An accurate understanding of reality is the essential foundation for good outcomes; good and bad are judged by consistency with how reality works and what it rewards and punishes.

mechanisms.name: Principles as stress-tested probabilistic claims
mechanisms.paraphrase: Nothing is certain, only highly probable; publishing the principles and having skeptics test them raises the probability they are right; the culture's theory is treated as tested over 40 years.

mechanisms.name: Five personal practices
mechanisms.paraphrase: Form independent opinions; stress-test them with the smartest people who can show where you are wrong, attending to their reasoning not conclusions; be wary of overconfidence and good at not knowing; experience the results of decisions and reflect on them.

mechanisms.name: Opinions should be costly
mechanisms.paraphrase: Markets charge for bad opinions while elsewhere opinions are free; he therefore limits bets to things he is confident in and avoids inadvertent bets (endnote 7).

mechanisms.name: Pain + Reflection = Progress
mechanisms.paraphrase: Pain signals a barrier; reflecting on it rather than fighting or fleeing is where most learning comes from.

mechanisms.name: Second- and third-order consequences
mechanisms.paraphrase: Decisions judged on first-order consequences alone usually fail; weigh later-order effects.

mechanisms.name: No-excuses accountability; luck vs skill
mechanisms.paraphrase: Blaming outcomes on others is at variance with reality; over a large sample of decisions luck cancels and skill dominates (endnote 38).

mechanisms.name: Ego barrier
mechanisms.paraphrase: Defensive emotional reactions stop people from examining their weaknesses or letting others examine them; since one's own weaknesses are hard to see, others' probing is essential.

mechanisms.name: Blind spot barrier
mechanisms.paraphrase: Two reasons you cannot see your own weaknesses: ego barriers, and a missing ability is like a missing sense; so others must show you.

mechanisms.name: The two yous
mechanisms.paraphrase: You(1) designs and oversees the plan; you(2) is one resource within it; you(1) must assess you(2) objectively and replace you(2) in any role you(2) does badly.

mechanisms.name: Machine metaphor and feedback loop
mechanisms.paraphrase: Goals determine a machine of design plus people; compare its outcomes to goals; when they diverge, change the design or the people; higher-level thinking is looking down on the machine and yourself in it.

mechanisms.name: Feedback-loop frequency sets evolution rate
mechanisms.paraphrase: Many high-quality feedback loops give a steep improvement trajectory; few or poor ones give decline; managing feedback loops is what separates great organizations from bad ones.

mechanisms.name: 5-Step Process
mechanisms.paraphrase: Goals, identify and don't tolerate problems, diagnose root causes, design plans, do tasks; keep steps distinct; iterative; each needs different abilities; usable as a diagnostic of which step you fail at.

mechanisms.name: Self-assessment must cite evidence
mechanisms.paraphrase: Each self-rating is followed by: how confident are you, and why — a demonstrated track record or believable people having told you.

mechanisms.name: Root cause vs proximate cause
mechanisms.paraphrase: Proximate causes are actions (verbs); root causes are reasons, usually traits (adjectives); only removing root causes removes problems.

mechanisms.name: Problem precision and problem vs cause
mechanisms.paraphrase: Specify exactly which problem, with whom, in what circumstances; a cause such as lack of sleep is not the problem, the suboptimal outcome is.

mechanisms.name: External benchmarks on execution
mechanisms.paraphrase: Set clear benchmarks and ideally have someone other than yourself measure whether the plan is being followed.

mechanisms.name: Track record built from many decisions
mechanisms.paraphrase: The sheer number of decisions gives ample opportunity to build a track record; start modest and raise goals as the record justifies confidence.

mechanisms.name: Right to understand, duty to speak
mechanisms.paraphrase: Everyone has the right to understand what makes sense and no one may hold a critical opinion without voicing it.

mechanisms.name: Meritocracy of thought
mechanisms.paraphrase: All can speak openly and views are judged on their merits; extreme openness plus merit-judging is the stated reason the firm performs well.

mechanisms.name: Radical transparency
mechanisms.paraphrase: Give people direct exposure to what is going on so they form their own views; candid question-and-answer lets people probe your reasoning.

mechanisms.name: Record and share meetings
mechanisms.paraphrase: Almost all meetings are recorded and the tapes shared with relevant people, barring confidential content.

mechanisms.name: Mistake culture
mechanisms.paraphrase: It is acceptable to make mistakes but unacceptable not to identify, analyze and learn from them.

mechanisms.name: Patterns of mistakes reveal weaknesses
mechanisms.paraphrase: A repeated pattern of mistakes signals a weakness, which is either a learning deficit (slowly fixable) or an ability deficit (design around it).

mechanisms.name: Accurate/inaccurate instead of blame/credit
mechanisms.paraphrase: Feedback is framed as accuracy for future improvement, not punishment for the past; blame-and-credit thinking blocks the learning loop.

mechanisms.name: Don't depersonalize mistakes
mechanisms.paraphrase: Diagnoses must name the specific person responsible; saying 'we' hides the cause and tests whether a person puts improvement above ego.

mechanisms.name: Write down weaknesses
mechanisms.paraphrase: Record your own and others' weaknesses so they are acknowledged and can be evolved past.

mechanisms.name: Reflect on pain with believable others
mechanisms.paraphrase: When in pain, calm down, find the cause, ask objective believable people to help, and don't let ego barriers block it.

mechanisms.name: Penalize covering up mistakes
mechanisms.paraphrase: Hiding a mistake is the worst mistake; mistakes are highlighted, diagnosed, and the lesson added to the procedures manual.

mechanisms.name: Issues log is mandatory
mechanisms.paraphrase: The issues log is the main tool for mistake-based learning and its use is enforced rather than optional.

mechanisms.name: Get in synch
mechanisms.paraphrase: Constantly reconcile views on what is true and what to do through asking, debating, discussing and teaching.

mechanisms.name: Assertive and open-minded
mechanisms.paraphrase: Aim to find what is true rather than win; being shown wrong is more valuable than being right.

mechanisms.name: Earned right to an opinion
mechanisms.paraphrase: Ask whether you have earned the right to an opinion; opinions are cheap so bad ones abound.

mechanisms.name: Right to ask questions
mechanisms.paraphrase: Everyone always has the right to ask questions.

mechanisms.name: Open- vs closed-minded
mechanisms.paraphrase: Open-minded people ask and know their knowledge is small; closed-minded people tell regardless of knowledge.

mechanisms.name: Commentators from the stands
mechanisms.paraphrase: Be wary of the arrogant intellectual who comments without having played on the field.

mechanisms.name: Explain reasoning; appeal to more-believable arbiters
mechanisms.paraphrase: Responsible parties must openly explain their reasoning; disagreements are appealed to the boss or an agreed knowledgeable group including people more believable and senior, who must judge objectively.

mechanisms.name: Untapped potential in disagreement
mechanisms.paraphrase: Disagreement between thoughtful people is a major source of learning that most people avoid or turn into a fight.

mechanisms.name: Debate whether to debate
mechanisms.paraphrase: If people disagree on whether an issue merits debate, it is debated, otherwise the boss gets a de facto veto.

mechanisms.name: Many ways to skin a cat
mechanisms.paraphrase: Judge responsible parties by whether the job is done well, not whether it is done your way.

mechanisms.name: Evaluate decisions in context
mechanisms.paraphrase: A challenged decision is judged within the decision-maker's broader vision, not as an isolated detail.

mechanisms.name: Not rule by referendum
mechanisms.paraphrase: Open debate supplies alternative views to the decision-maker and helps assess people over time; it does not make decisions by vote.

mechanisms.name: Debate, discussion or teaching by believability
mechanisms.paraphrase: Choose the mode by goal and relative believability: debate among equals, discussion across levels, teaching between levels; say which you are having.

mechanisms.name: Involve the most relevant people
mechanisms.paraphrase: Best-answer communication involves managers, direct reports and agreed experts; people should weigh their own believability before probing; escalate if not in synch.

mechanisms.name: Tiger Woods test
mechanisms.paraphrase: Do not weight a novice's and a champion's views equally, but the novice should keep questioning until convinced, without overblown confidence.

mechanisms.name: Opinions weighted by track record
mechanisms.paraphrase: Views without track records are not equal to views with them; all views are considered but placed in the context of experience and record; the test is whether you can handle the responsibility.

mechanisms.name: Hierarchy of merit
mechanisms.paraphrase: A hierarchy of merit is essential to a meritocracy of ideas and to getting work done.

mechanisms.name: Believability
mechanisms.paraphrase: Believability is the probability a person's view is right, roughly assessed from the quality of their reasoning and their track record; ask 'Why should I believe you?' and 'Why should I believe myself?'

mechanisms.name: Track record gates opinions
mechanisms.paraphrase: With a demonstrated track record you may hold an opinion on how to do the thing; without one you may hold theories and questions.

mechanisms.name: Believability tiers and confidence labeling
mechanisms.paraphrase: Repeated success at the thing plus great explanations when probed is most believable; one of the two is somewhat; neither is least. Ideas are still judged on merit so people can build records; assessments are visible; state confidence honestly, suggestion vs conviction.

mechanisms.name: Right person to answer
mechanisms.paraphrase: Before answering a question, consider whether you are the responsible party or right person to answer it.

mechanisms.name: Meeting responsible party
mechanisms.paraphrase: Every meeting has a named responsible party who decides its purpose and runs it.

mechanisms.name: Choose participants by value, not agreement
mechanisms.paraphrase: Limit participants to those who add most; the worst selection criterion is whether their conclusions match yours.

mechanisms.name: Small group of 3-5
mechanisms.paraphrase: Three to five smart conceptual open-minded people produce the best answers; a single such decision-maker is next; a large leaderless group is worst.

mechanisms.name: 1+1=3 with diminishing returns
mechanisms.paraphrase: Good collaborators are about three times as effective as alone, with diminishing and then negative returns as the group grows.

mechanisms.name: Two levels: case and principle
mechanisms.paraphrase: Discuss both the case at hand and the principle or machine it exemplifies, which handles the case, improves the machine and tests the principle.

mechanisms.name: Completion in writing
mechanisms.paraphrase: End discussions by stating conclusions, working theories and assigned to-dos, written down for later use.

mechanisms.name: No loss of responsibility in groups
mechanisms.paraphrase: Group decisions must assign personal responsibility for who does what.

mechanisms.name: Right to debate vs right to decide
mechanisms.paraphrase: Authority is assigned to individuals by assessed ability; they are accountable for outcomes; a responsible party may decide against knowledgeable disagreement after weighing it; an explicit decision hierarchy ideally based on merit.

mechanisms.name: Escalate to a believable third party
mechanisms.paraphrase: If two people cannot get in synch, they agree on a manager or other believable person or group to resolve it objectively; called key to maintaining the meritocracy of ideas.

mechanisms.name: Inevitable responsible party
mechanisms.paraphrase: The responsible party is whoever bears the consequences; delegation does not remove responsibility for choosing and incentivizing delegates.

mechanisms.name: You get what you deserve over time
mechanisms.paraphrase: Results reflect how you and your people handle things; hold yourself and others accountable.

mechanisms.name: Most important RPs are highest in the pyramid
mechanisms.paraphrase: Those responsible for goals, outcomes and machines matter most to choose and manage well.

mechanisms.name: Track records in hiring
mechanisms.paraphrase: Pay attention to candidates' track records; ask for past reviews from believable people and documented evidence; check references.

mechanisms.name: Performance within an outstanding peer group
mechanisms.paraphrase: The clearest demonstration of excellence is outstanding performance among outstanding peers.

mechanisms.name: Candidates hear the tapes
mechanisms.paraphrase: Candidates are shown the principles and listen to recorded meetings to see how the firm actually operates.

mechanisms.name: Experts are harsher critics
mechanisms.paraphrase: An excellent practitioner judges another practitioner more critically and accurately than a novice does.

mechanisms.name: Large sample size of outcomes
mechanisms.paraphrase: Compare outcomes to goals constantly so the sample is large enough to separate one-off errors from root causes.

mechanisms.name: Machine-level and case-level discussion
mechanisms.paraphrase: When a problem occurs discuss why the machine produced it and separately what to do now.

mechanisms.name: Explain logic; mutual accountability to principles
mechanisms.paraphrase: Rules come with their reasoning; each person must judge whether they agree and say why, and hold others to the principles.

mechanisms.name: Daily accountability builds the sample
mechanisms.paraphrase: Holding people accountable daily builds a sample that reveals problems early.

mechanisms.name: Broken contract vs no contract
mechanisms.paraphrase: You can only hold people to expectations that were made explicit; a missing contract is a design fault to fix.

mechanisms.name: Agreed goals displayed
mechanisms.paraphrase: Goals, tasks and responsibilities are shown to the whole department monthly or quarterly so it is clear who is keeping up their end.

mechanisms.name: No vague 'we should'
mechanisms.paraphrase: Replace 'we should' with named believable responsible parties who determine what should be done.

mechanisms.name: Daily updates
mechanisms.paraphrase: Five-minute daily notes of what was done, planned, problems, questions and observations.

mechanisms.name: Confidence learned, not presumed
mechanisms.paraphrase: Trust in a person's handling of responsibilities is built from direct experience over time.

mechanisms.name: Vary involvement by confidence
mechanisms.paraphrase: Probe more where things look suspicious and less where probing has built confidence; scan tool outputs such as issues log, metrics, daily updates and checklists.

mechanisms.name: Escalation preserves attribution
mechanisms.paraphrase: A responsible party must say whether they can handle the job; a boss doing it silently destroys the attribution of success and failure.

mechanisms.name: Escalation button
mechanisms.paraphrase: An explicit tool so a manager knows a report is escalating rather than merely reporting a problem.

mechanisms.name: Point of the pyramid
mechanisms.paraphrase: Cross-departmental issues go to the person above both parties, who has the perspective to weigh trade-offs.

mechanisms.name: Two-way probing
mechanisms.paraphrase: Probe your reports and have them probe you; probing surfaces hidden discontent and makes people players rather than spectators.

mechanisms.name: Probe two levels down
mechanisms.paraphrase: Know your reports' reports and invite them to bring disagreements with their bosses to you.

mechanisms.name: Independent audit
mechanisms.paraphrase: Ask the hard questions and independently audit rather than letting people off the hook.

mechanisms.name: Trust earned through checking
mechanisms.paraphrase: Don't assume answers are correct; double-check, and trust in a person's statements is gained or lost through that process.

mechanisms.name: Transparent probing
mechanisms.paraphrase: Probing is done in the open so others can assess its quality, reinforcing the transparency culture.

mechanisms.name: Accurate assessments
mechanisms.paraphrase: Precise personnel evaluations take time and back-and-forth; consult other believable people; don't be overconfident.

mechanisms.name: Evaluation tools
mechanisms.paraphrase: Performance surveys, metrics and formal reviews document all aspects of performance.

mechanisms.name: Baseball cards / believability matrixes
mechanisms.paraphrase: A per-person card of performance statistics, like a baseball card, built from ratings, forced rankings, metrics, results and credentials; used transparently for role assignment, compensation, promotion and cuts, and passed to prospective managers.

mechanisms.name: Hypothesis about a person, tested iteratively
mechanisms.paraphrase: State your theory of a person's values, abilities and skills, share it, test it with assignments, and revise on observed performance.

mechanisms.name: Accurate criticism is most valuable
mechanisms.paraphrase: Weaknesses are profiled accurately; nothing is more valuable than accurate criticism.

mechanisms.name: Track record as level and slope, not wiggles
mechanisms.paraphrase: Reviews aggregate many probed cases into patterns; everyone fails sometimes; a track record is the level and steepness of the trajectories a person owns, not the fluctuations.

mechanisms.name: Career path emerges from assessment
mechanisms.paraphrase: Roles are not planned but evolve from discovered strengths and weaknesses through periodic mini-reviews and major reviews, with new assignments as tests.

mechanisms.name: Patterns, not single events
mechanisms.paraphrase: Distinguish 'you made a bad decision' from 'you are a bad decision-maker', which only a pattern shows; some qualities need one observation, others five to ten.

mechanisms.name: Learning vs ability
mechanisms.paraphrase: Poor performance is due either to inadequate training or experience, which can be fixed, or inadequate ability, which cannot.

mechanisms.name: Non-hierarchical assessment
mechanisms.paraphrase: Evaluations run in both directions and must be reconciled; overconfidence and failing to get in synch are the two big assessment errors.

mechanisms.name: Agreed weaknesses go on the card
mechanisms.paraphrase: When both parties genuinely agree on a weakness it is probably true; write it on the baseball card.

mechanisms.name: By-and-large judgments of people
mechanisms.paraphrase: Aim for a mutually agreed high-confidence by-and-large understanding, not proof beyond doubt.

mechanisms.name: Assessment horizon
mechanisms.paraphrase: Rough assessment after 6-12 months of close contact and tests, confident after about 18 months; ratios of 1:5 to 1:10 keep contact sufficient.

mechanisms.name: Two believable trainers triangulate
mechanisms.paraphrase: At least two believable trainers per trainee so views of the trainee can be triangulated.

mechanisms.name: Everything is a case study
mechanisms.paraphrase: Ask what each situation is a case of and which principles apply.

mechanisms.name: Acceptable vs unacceptable mistakes
mechanisms.paraphrase: Allow mistakes whose damage is bounded ('scratch or dent the car') but not ones that could total it.

mechanisms.name: Separate what's true from what to do
mechanisms.paraphrase: Deciding what is true takes months and a large sample; deciding what to do takes hours or days.

mechanisms.name: Sort out and record reasons
mechanisms.paraphrase: When someone doesn't fit a role, move them out quickly and record the reasons on their baseball card.

mechanisms.name: Keeping the unsuited erodes meritocracy
mechanisms.paraphrase: Retaining a person unsuited to a job is worse than firing because everyone bears the consequences and it erodes meritocracy.

mechanisms.name: Do not lower the bar
mechanisms.paraphrase: People who cannot reach the standard of excellence and radical truth in acceptable time must go.

mechanisms.name: Above or below the bar
mechanisms.paraphrase: The key perception is whether something is good enough or not; it requires synthesis.

mechanisms.name: Accountable for raising and escalating complaints
mechanisms.paraphrase: Did someone think something was wrong, did it lead to discussion, and if not did they escalate; that is the expected sequence.

mechanisms.name: Leader must encourage disagreement
mechanisms.paraphrase: The leader must invite disagreement and be impartial or open-minded.

mechanisms.name: Those closest know best
mechanisms.paraphrase: People closest to a job have perspectives essential to improvement.

mechanisms.name: Movie vs script
mechanisms.paraphrase: Perceive problems by comparing actual operation and outcomes to the visualized expectation, e.g. an expected improvement band; deviation signals a root cause.

mechanisms.name: Use specific names
mechanisms.paraphrase: The anonymous 'we' and 'they' mask responsibility; say who should, who erred, who did well.

mechanisms.name: Issues log as scored ledger
mechanisms.paraphrase: Anything that went wrong is logged with frank assessment of individual contributions; counts and types become performance metrics; usage is rewarded and non-use punished: an unlogged failure means big trouble, a logged and diagnosed one is likely praised.

mechanisms.name: Metrics, grader-bias detection, forced rankings
mechanisms.paraphrase: Metrics must not be gamed and a single metric misleads; lenient graders are detected by their average grade; forced rankings grade on a curve; metrics allowing independent grading across departments are especially valuable; use metrics to ask questions.

mechanisms.name: Problem states
mechanisms.paraphrase: Problems are unidentified, identified without a plan, identified with a plan, or solved; identified-without-a-plan is worst for morale.

mechanisms.name: Problems are machine outputs
mechanisms.paraphrase: Every problem is a manifestation of root causes in the design or the people; diagnose both.

mechanisms.name: Diagnostic question script
mechanisms.paraphrase: Ask: what suboptimality occurred; who is the responsible party; what was the mental map of how it should have worked; what broke, design or behavior; proximate vs root causes; is it consistent with prior patterns and what systematic change follows; 10-20 minutes, done constantly.

mechanisms.name: Root cause is a reason
mechanisms.paraphrase: Keep asking why; root causes are described with adjectives and usually trace to specific people, who must be diagnosed as accurately as equipment.

mechanisms.name: Locate failure in the 5-Step Process
mechanisms.paraphrase: Chronic failure is traced to a step and the abilities it needs: goals (vision, values), perceiving (perception, synthesis, intolerance of badness), diagnosis (logic, assertiveness, open-mindedness), design (creativity, visualization), tasks (determination, discipline).

mechanisms.name: Collaborative diagnosis
mechanisms.paraphrase: Don't just give a verdict; there is a high probability you don't know the answer, so explore theories with relevant others.

mechanisms.name: Diagnoses produce written theories
mechanisms.paraphrase: Every diagnosis yields at least written theories of root causes, kept as a collection of synthesized dots for pattern-finding.

mechanisms.name: Don't over-squeeze one dot
mechanisms.paraphrase: A single outcome tells only so much; collect many dots quickly and triangulate with others' dots into a pointillist picture.

mechanisms.name: Continuous synthesis
mechanisms.paraphrase: Categorize and observe the evolution of parts of the machine over time to see whether they improve or worsen.

mechanisms.name: No Monday-morning quarterbacking
mechanisms.paraphrase: Judge a past decision by what could reasonably have been known at the time and what a quality person should have done.

mechanisms.name: Identify violated principles
mechanisms.paraphrase: Determine which principles applied and whether they would have helped; improve the principles.

mechanisms.name: Same people, same things, same results
mechanisms.paraphrase: Expect no change in results without a change in people or process.

mechanisms.name: Drilldown
mechanisms.paraphrase: List specific problems, then in a separate session identify root causes, then design a plan; implement with monthly to-do lists, open progress meetings, metrics on commitments and a publicly posted plan; include the people under scrutiny.

mechanisms.name: Go back before going forward
mechanisms.paraphrase: Diagnose what went right and wrong and tell the story of how you got here; new employees listen to recorded tapes of the story.

mechanisms.name: Above and below the line
mechanisms.paraphrase: Keep discussion moving through main points to a synthesis, dipping into details only to illuminate them.

mechanisms.name: Design a machine to produce outcomes
mechanisms.paraphrase: For an ongoing mission build a machine of people and their interactions; keep comparing its outcomes to goals.

mechanisms.name: Visualize alternative machines
mechanisms.paraphrase: Imagine different configurations and people, play each forward month by month, then choose.

mechanisms.name: Second- and third-order consequences
mechanisms.paraphrase: Later-order effects can reverse first-order desirability (the '1.6 effect' in hiring).

mechanisms.name: Organize around goals, not tasks
mechanisms.paraphrase: Separate departments per goal so incentives don't conflict and diagnosis of resources is clear.

mechanisms.name: Overseen by a believable person
mechanisms.paraphrase: Everyone must be overseen by a believable person with high standards; don't just trust.

mechanisms.name: Span-of-control limits
mechanisms.paraphrase: Ratios of managers to reports and to people two levels down of at most 1:10, preferably 1:5, to preserve quality communication.

mechanisms.name: Clear reporting lines
mechanisms.paraphrase: Single reporting lines that don't cross; dual reporting muddies accountability.

mechanisms.name: Clover-leaf design
mechanisms.paraphrase: Two or three responsible parties with overlapping believabilities who challenge and check each other and escalate what they can't resolve.

mechanisms.name: Department slip
mechanisms.paraphrase: Support departments provide support and feedback; they don't set the vision for what they support.

mechanisms.name: Responsibilities by ability, not title
mechanisms.paraphrase: Assign responsibility based on workflow design and people's abilities rather than job titles.

mechanisms.name: Procedures manual fed by the issues log
mechanisms.paraphrase: A living manual of how the machine works, incorporating diagnosed mistakes so they aren't repeated.

mechanisms.name: Checklists
mechanisms.paraphrase: Capture assigned tasks on checklists so completion is confirmed; checklists are not a substitute for responsibility.

mechanisms.name: Double-do
mechanisms.paraphrase: Two people independently do the same mission-critical task and results are compared; catches more errors than checking and reveals performance differences.

mechanisms.name: Controls so trust is never the issue
mechanisms.paraphrase: Many people cheat given the chance; security controls are a professional necessity, not an insult.

mechanisms.name: Independent audit
mechanisms.paraphrase: Auditors report outside the audited department and audit procedures are not disclosed to those audited.

mechanisms.name: Laws need policemen
mechanisms.paraphrase: Rules are pointless without auditors to enforce them.

mechanisms.name: Low probability of holding the best answer
mechanisms.paraphrase: You probably don't have the best answer, and can't be confident you do unless believable people test you.

mechanisms.name: What don't I know?
mechanisms.paraphrase: Ask what you don't know and what to do about it; ask believable people for their reasoning, not conclusions.

mechanisms.name: Assess the probability you have the answers
mechanisms.paraphrase: Successful people ask whether they know the important questions and objectively assess the probability that they have the answers.

mechanisms.name: Questions for all, opinions for the believable
mechanisms.paraphrase: Everyone may hold questions and theories; only believable people may hold opinions; others may voice views if they flag uncertainty.

mechanisms.name: Triangulate with three believable people
mechanisms.paraphrase: No important decision without asking at least three believable people, assessing their reasoning and having them probe yours.

mechanisms.name: Decisions as expected-value calculations
mechanisms.paraphrase: Weigh probabilities and payoffs of consequences; make the probability of ruin nil.

mechanisms.name: Cost of a bad decision
mechanisms.paraphrase: A bad decision costs at least as much as a good one earns, so knowing what you don't know is as valuable as knowing.

mechanisms.name: Asymmetric bets
mechanisms.paraphrase: Seek chances with little to lose and much to gain even at low probability; all decisions are risk/reward bets.

mechanisms.name: Raise the probability of being right
mechanisms.paraphrase: People voice opinions at just over 50% confidence; investigating and checking with others to reach 85% is worth more than moving from 45% to 51%.

mechanisms.name: 15 or more uncorrelated bets
mechanisms.paraphrase: Don't bet too much on any one thing; hold many good uncorrelated bets.

mechanisms.name: Fewer than five things matter
mechanisms.paraphrase: Most decisions turn on fewer than five considerations; marginal study past a point has limited gain.

mechanisms.name: Timing of decisions
mechanisms.paraphrase: Weigh the marginal gain of more information against the marginal cost of delay.

mechanisms.name: More pros than cons
mechanisms.paraphrase: The best choice has more pros than cons, not zero cons; distrust those who oppose anything with a flaw.

mechanisms.name: Possibilities need probabilities
mechanisms.paraphrase: Raising possibilities without likelihoods wrecks prioritization; almost anything is possible, so every possibility must carry a probability.

mechanisms.name: By and large
mechanisms.paraphrase: Treat a mostly-true statement as true enough rather than derailing into exceptions; 'not totally true' usually means true enough.

mechanisms.name: Connect the dots over time
mechanisms.paraphrase: Categorize every outcome by type and quality and chart each type over time; about five dots of a type are needed to find a root cause.

mechanisms.name: Level over rate of change
mechanisms.paraphrase: Improving but still below the bar is not good enough; what matters is being on a trajectory to cross the acceptable bar in acceptable time.

mechanisms.name: Escalate insufficient solutions
mechanisms.paraphrase: If your best solution isn't good enough, think harder or escalate that you can't produce one.

mechanisms.name: No opt-outs
mechanisms.paraphrase: Allowing people to opt out of exploring their weaknesses would create two sets of rules and endanger the radically honest system.

mechanisms.name: Truth over happiness
mechanisms.paraphrase: The manager's job is to get at truth and excellence, not to make people happy; the best answers over the long run make the right people happiest.

mechanisms.name: Believability-weighted voting (endnote 54)
mechanisms.paraphrase: He once considered a voting system based on a believability matrix; probably impractical, but it expresses the merit-based decision-making the process aims at; probing is meant to assess work quality over time, not to second-guess each decision.

mechanisms.name: Overabundance of confident bad opinions (endnote 53)
mechanisms.paraphrase: People confidently express poorly formed opinions and rarely learn from disagreement; open-mindedly exploring disagreements would radically increase learning.

mechanisms.name: Luck cancels over a large sample (endnote 38)
mechanisms.paraphrase: Over many decisions, like many poker hands, luck cancels and skill dominates outcomes; a superior decision-maker produces superior outcomes.

mechanisms.name: Learning via rewards and punishments (endnote 64)
mechanisms.paraphrase: People learn principles by experiencing the rewards and punishments of their actions; clearly designated responsibility sharpens the cause-effect feedback.

mechanisms.name: Expected reward vs expected cost (endnote 47)
mechanisms.paraphrase: People stop caring to solve problems when expected reward is below expected cost, e.g. working for others' goals without supervision, reward or punishment.

mechanisms.name: Quick answers unexamined (endnote 14)
mechanisms.paraphrase: People quick to produce answers usually haven't thought about the ways they could be wrong.

mechanisms.name: Ask opposing believable people (endnote 30)
mechanisms.paraphrase: Ask believable people, especially those with opposing views who want truth rather than to be proven right, to help find root causes.

mechanisms.name: Believability (compact definition)
mechanisms.paraphrase: Believable parties are people who have repeatedly and successfully done the thing in question and can explain how they did it (Part II footnote 15).

mechanisms.name: Believability (full definition)
mechanisms.paraphrase: Believable people have a strong track record on the specific thing (at least three successes) and give great explanations of their approach when probed; believability is relative to the topic and to the other party.

mechanisms.name: Believability two-part test
mechanisms.paraphrase: Most believable opinions come from people who (1) have repeatedly and successfully accomplished the thing in question and (2) have demonstrated they can logically explain the cause-effect behind their conclusions; criteria must be objective and trusted by everybody, tracked systematically with Baseball Cards and the Dot Collector.

mechanisms.name: Believability grading rule
mechanisms.paraphrase: Neither criterion met: not believable; one met: somewhat believable; both met: most believable. Be wary of those who only comment from the stands.

mechanisms.name: Attribute-specific believability
mechanisms.paraphrase: A person has different believability weightings for different qualities (subject expertise, creativity, synthesis); weights come from peer ratings and tests; for each decision you choose which qualities matter.

mechanisms.name: Stress-test untested theories
mechanisms.paraphrase: Someone without a track record but with a logical, testable theory should have it tested rather than dismissed.

mechanisms.name: Weigh reasoning over conclusions
mechanisms.paraphrase: Pay more attention to the reasoning that led to a conclusion than to the conclusion itself; inexperienced people can have great ideas.

mechanisms.name: Declare confidence up front
mechanisms.paraphrase: Everyone should state how confident they are in an opinion; a suggestion and a firm belief must be presented differently.

mechanisms.name: Discount self-assessment
mechanisms.paraphrase: Statements beginning 'I think that I...' are discounted because people cannot assess themselves accurately; the body of evidence and others' input must be relied on instead.

mechanisms.name: Systematic capture of track records
mechanisms.paraphrase: Believability is assessed by capturing track records over time; evidence accumulates ('every day is not a new day') and is open to scrutiny through Baseball Cards and the Dot Collector.

mechanisms.name: Three-successes hiring test
mechanisms.paraphrase: Ask whether the person has done the thing successfully at least three times; if not, it is a lower-probability bet needing strong reasons.

mechanisms.name: Judge process and outcomes over time (poker analogy)
mechanisms.paraphrase: Never judge a player on one hand; look at how well someone does what they do and the outcomes produced over time; repeated bad reasoning plus bad outcomes is disqualifying.

mechanisms.name: Dots and at-bats
mechanisms.paraphrase: A dot is one observation paired with an inference about it; each dot is an at-bat, so evaluate on aggregates (batting average), never a single event.

mechanisms.name: Believability applies to management
mechanisms.paraphrase: An excellent skier makes a better ski coach than a novice; the right to judge others' work follows from track record.

mechanisms.name: Idea meritocracy formula
mechanisms.paraphrase: Idea Meritocracy = Radical Truth + Radical Transparency + Believability-Weighted Decision Making.

mechanisms.name: Three requirements of an idea meritocracy
mechanisms.paraphrase: Put honest thoughts on the table; have thoughtful disagreement; abide by agreed-upon ways of getting past disagreement.

mechanisms.name: Believability-weighted decision procedure
mechanisms.paraphrase: Everyone gives input; input is weighted by evidence; pick the qualities relevant to the decision; poll; compare equal-weighted and believability-weighted results; if they agree proceed, if not revisit the disagreement; the weighted vote supersedes the Responsible Party in some decision types, and RPs who overrule do so at their peril as a bet the results will judge.

mechanisms.name: Believability-weighted answer vs. boss vs. referendum
mechanisms.paraphrase: The believability-weighted answer is not always right but is more likely right than either the boss's answer or an equal-weighted referendum (2012 ECB example resolved with the Dot Collector).

mechanisms.name: Perils of believability weighting
mechanisms.paraphrase: Avoid over-valuing your own believability and failing to distinguish who is more or less credible; when disagreeing with believable people, explore their reasoning, apply shared principles, or work through the principle-level disagreement.

mechanisms.name: Choose a believable triangle
mechanisms.paraphrase: Pick about three believable people who care about the outcome and will disagree openly; compare the crowd's believability-weighted view with your own and ask why you differ; if unresolved, suspend judgment and go with the vote.

mechanisms.name: Do not poll randomly
mechanisms.paraphrase: Asking everyone's opinion regardless of believability is an unproductive waste; decision-seeking communication involves the most relevant people, educational communication a broader set.

mechanisms.name: The 5-Step Process
mechanisms.paraphrase: Clear goals; identify and do not tolerate problems; diagnose root causes; design a plan; push through; one step at a time, iterated; identify at which step chronic failures occur.

mechanisms.name: Proximate vs. root causes
mechanisms.paraphrase: Proximate causes are actions (verbs); root causes are qualities of people or design (adjectives); keep asking why until a root cause is reached.

mechanisms.name: Pain + Reflection = Progress
mechanisms.paraphrase: Pain signals something to learn; reflect during or after it; go toward pain rather than avoid it; organizationally, covering up mistakes is penalized and mistake logging is mandatory.

mechanisms.name: Machine metaphor
mechanisms.paraphrase: You are the designer and manager of a machine (design plus people) that converts goals into outcomes; compare outcomes to goals and modify the machine; an organization is a machine of culture and people.

mechanisms.name: Two purposes of every case
mechanisms.paraphrase: Each case should move you toward the goal and also train and test the machine; discuss the machine level and the case level separately; everything is a case study.

mechanisms.name: Machine diagnosis questions
mechanisms.paraphrase: Is the outcome good or bad; who is responsible; if bad, is the Responsible Party incapable and/or the design bad; how should the machine have worked; what broke; why; is it a pattern; how should people and machine evolve; which 5-step stage failed; which principles were violated; judge on what was knowable then; separate capacity from capability.

mechanisms.name: Drill-down technique
mechanisms.paraphrase: List problems specifically naming people; identify root causes by repeated why; create a plan with owners, metrics, timelines; execute and report planned vs. actual at least monthly with public accountability.

mechanisms.name: Designated problem-perceivers
mechanisms.paraphrase: Assign people the job of perceiving problems with independent reporting lines so they can report without fear; compare outcomes to the expected trajectory band; do not treat nobody worrying as evidence.

mechanisms.name: Thoughtful disagreement protocol
mechanisms.paraphrase: Aim to find which view is right, not to win; agree on the mode (open vs. persuade); each side gets two uninterrupted minutes; decide who is teacher, student, or peer by relative believability; the student must first try to understand the teacher.

mechanisms.name: Two-step decision making
mechanisms.paraphrase: First take in all relevant information, then decide; refusing to take in disconfirming information does not protect your ability to decide.

mechanisms.name: Escalate or vote
mechanisms.paraphrase: If a one-on-one dispute stalls, escalate to a mutually agreed believable person higher in the chain; if a group stalls, the meeting owner takes a believability-weighted vote.

mechanisms.name: Ego barrier
mechanisms.paraphrase: A subliminal need to be right and capable fights the logical higher-level self; the two 'yous' compete for control.

mechanisms.name: Blind-spot barrier
mechanisms.paraphrase: Differences in wiring make each person systematically blind to some things; closed-mindedness is costly because you never see what you miss.

mechanisms.name: Blind-spot remedies
mechanisms.paraphrase: Keep a written list of your blind-spot areas and do not decide in them without consulting others; if several believable people say you are wrong and you alone disagree, assume you are biased, switch to asking questions, compare believabilities, bring in a neutral party.

mechanisms.name: Evidence-based decision tools
mechanisms.paraphrase: Use decision-making tools with a better track record than yourself (computerized systems that capture more logic, process more information, and are not emotionally hijacked); know when to stop fighting and trust the process.

mechanisms.name: Expected-value decisions
mechanisms.paraphrase: Decide by probability times reward minus probability times penalty; a 20 percent chance at 10x payoff has positive EV; it is not always right to bet on the most probable outcome if you can cover the loss.

mechanisms.name: Raising probability of being right is always valuable
mechanisms.paraphrase: Moving from 51 to 85 percent is worth seventeen times moving from 49 to 51 percent; knowing when not to bet is as important as choosing bets; best choices have more pros than cons, not zero cons.

mechanisms.name: Value of information vs. cost of delay
mechanisms.paraphrase: Prioritize by weighing the marginal benefit of more information against the cost of not deciding; keep must-dos above the bar; do not mistake possibilities for probabilities.

mechanisms.name: Open-mindedness signs
mechanisms.paraphrase: Seven cues: wanting ideas challenged vs. not; asking questions vs. making statements; understanding others vs. being understood; genuine vs. perfunctory 'I could be wrong'; letting others speak vs. blocking; holding two thoughts at once; humility from having crashed.

mechanisms.name: Practices of radical open-mindedness
mechanisms.paraphrase: Accept not knowing; learn then decide; do not worry about looking good; you cannot output without input; suspend judgment to empathize; seek the best answer not your own; know whether you are arguing or understanding based on believability.

mechanisms.name: Synthesis through time (dots)
mechanisms.paraphrase: Categorize outcomes by type and quality, plot them over time, judge trajectories against acceptable and excellent bars, be imprecise, apply 80/20.

mechanisms.name: Principles to algorithms
mechanisms.paraphrase: Slow down, write the criteria used as a principle, refine when outcomes arrive; encode principles so a computer evaluates them against data; test rules on history; thinking leads to principles leads to algorithms.

mechanisms.name: Caution about machine-learned rules
mechanisms.paraphrase: Distinguish expert systems (rules you understand) from mimicking and data mining (rules you do not); unexplained rules are dangerous when the future differs from the past.

mechanisms.name: Self-reinforcing evolutionary loop
mechanisms.paraphrase: Independent thinkers; idea meritocracy principles; principles written down and encoded in computers; decisions made by them; successes and failures produce more principles; repeat.

mechanisms.name: Dot Collector
mechanisms.paraphrase: Meeting app where participants give each other positive or negative dots on dozens of attributes in a live grid; gives GPS-style individual coaching; flags nubby questions and alerts you when you disagree with the believability-weighted majority; polls yes/no or numeric and reports equal-weighted and believability-weighted results; accumulates hundreds of data points per person per attribute.

mechanisms.name: Baseball Cards
mechanisms.paraphrase: Per-person profile of strengths and weaknesses with the evidence behind them, built from meeting dots, reviews, tests, and choices, combined by algorithms whose logic is vetted by the people rated; used in meetings to weigh whoever is speaking and as the spec for a role; the rated person compares it with their self-view.

mechanisms.name: People Profile
mechanisms.paraphrase: Text summary distilled from a person's Baseball Card.

mechanisms.name: Combinator
mechanisms.paraphrase: Searches Baseball Card data: enter people who fit an image, it extracts their key attributes and finds similar people; also generates job specifications.

mechanisms.name: Issue Log
mechanisms.paraphrase: Mandatory primary tool for recording mistakes and bad outcomes with severity and the responsible person; provides diagnostic paths and yields metrics on counts and types of problems and who causes and fixes them; originated as a trading error log.

mechanisms.name: Pain Button
mechanisms.paraphrase: App to record emotions at the moment of pain, reflect later with guided questions, specify an action plan, and track frequency, causes, follow-through, and results; entries can be shared or kept private.

mechanisms.name: Dispute Resolver
mechanisms.paraphrase: Guides disputants through questions toward resolution; locates believable people to judge whether a disagreement deserves escalation; makes clear that holding a different view obliges you to surface it; prevents the more powerful from pulling rank.

mechanisms.name: Daily Update Tool
mechanisms.paraphrase: Each direct report writes 10-15 minutes daily on what they did, issues, and reflections, plus morale, workload, and items to escalate; software pulls these into a dashboard with metrics; the manager triangulates updates to find threads to pull.

mechanisms.name: Contract Tool
mechanisms.paraphrase: Records explicit commitments between people (who asked, who must deliver) so both sides can monitor them; implicit contracts are worthless.

mechanisms.name: Process Flow Diagram
mechanisms.paraphrase: Flowchart of the organization as a machine showing roles, responsibilities, and how work flows to outcomes, with drill-down and links into Baseball Cards; exists for every department.

mechanisms.name: Policy and Procedures Manuals
mechanisms.paraphrase: A living compendium of codified organizational learning consulted like an operating manual; policies are natural extensions of principles; exceptions are rare, proposed in writing, and decided by the Management Committee.

mechanisms.name: Metrics
mechanisms.paraphrase: Four steps: know the goal, understand the process, identify the key points to measure, build levers tied to those metrics; cascade from CEO level to each person; the test is whether they say what and who is doing well or poorly.

mechanisms.name: Checklists
mechanisms.paraphrase: Capture assigned tasks; completion percentages become a metric; not a substitute for whole-job responsibility.

mechanisms.name: Coach
mechanisms.paraphrase: Library of common situations ('ones of those') linked to the relevant principles; users rate the advice, which improves the tool.

mechanisms.name: Virtual-learning case studies
mechanisms.paraphrase: Recorded meetings turned into cases with questions, pauses, and feedback, tailored to each person's believabilities, producing data on how people think.

mechanisms.name: Five purposes of the toolset
mechanisms.paraphrase: Learn what people are like; share what people are like; personalized training; guidance and oversight in specific situations; sort people into the right roles or out.

mechanisms.name: Pattern-level scoring from many small observations
mechanisms.paraphrase: Evaluate on aggregates of dots rather than single events; patterns, not incidents, are the unit of judgment.

mechanisms.name: Clear, impartial, predetermined metrics with consequences
mechanisms.paraphrase: The clearer the rules, the less argument; metrics can feed an algorithm that assigns consequences such as bonus points or pay, weighted by importance, used with discretion and refined over time.

mechanisms.name: Compensation loosely tied to metrics
mechanisms.paraphrase: Tie performance metrics at least loosely to compensation; pay for the person, not the job.

mechanisms.name: Rater-bias controls
mechanisms.paraphrase: Check each grader's average grade to detect easy or hard graders; use forced rankings (grading on a curve); prefer metrics that allow independent grading across departments.

mechanisms.name: Self-report discounted (301 percent)
mechanisms.paraphrase: Asking everyone what share of results they produced summed to 301 percent; self-assessments are not evidence.

mechanisms.name: Mandatory error logging
mechanisms.paraphrase: Not facing up to a mistake is among the worst mistakes; Issue Log use is mandatory; errors carry severity and owner.

mechanisms.name: Public progress accountability
mechanisms.paraphrase: Report planned vs. actual progress at least monthly and hold people publicly accountable; transparency lets everyone follow the discussion and the tape so justice is enforced by visibility.

mechanisms.name: Double-do rather than double-check
mechanisms.paraphrase: Have two people independently do mission-critical tasks to produce two answers; differences reveal performance; an auditor must be capable of doing the work.

mechanisms.name: Sampling instead of surveillance
mechanisms.paraphrase: Review a statistically reliable sample of cases with enough probing that people cannot hide.

mechanisms.name: Time-boxed assessment
mechanisms.paraphrase: Six to twelve months to roughly assess a person, about eighteen months for confidence; then train, guardrail, or remove.

mechanisms.name: Assessor track records
mechanisms.paraphrase: Capture data on the track records of the people making subjective interpretations (interviewers) to make subjective judgment scientific.

mechanisms.name: Override as a scored bet
mechanisms.paraphrase: A Responsible Party who bets against the believability-weighted consensus makes a bold statement that the results will prove right or wrong.

mechanisms.name: Incentives aligned with the whole
mechanisms.paraphrase: Individual incentives must be aligned with the group's goals; reward what works for the whole.

mechanisms.name: Accurate/inaccurate replaces blame/credit
mechanisms.paraphrase: Reframe feedback as accurate or inaccurate rather than blame or credit so mistakes can be surfaced and learned from.

mechanisms.name: Controls against dishonesty
mechanisms.paraphrase: Assume some people will cheat if they can: investigate and say so; auditors report outside the audited unit with procedures kept secret; audit the auditors; beware rubber-stamping; use visible consequences to deter.

mechanisms.name: Responsible Parties decide
mechanisms.paraphrase: Decisions sit with Responsible Parties chosen by believability for the goal or machine; the ultimate RP bears the consequences; everyone reports to someone.

mechanisms.name: Known locus of authority
mechanisms.paraphrase: It must be known where ultimate decision-making authority lies, i.e., how far the power of argument carries relative to assigned authority.

mechanisms.name: Explicit decision rights and vote weights
mechanisms.paraphrase: Make clear how much weight each person's vote has so that unresolved disagreement has a defined resolution.

mechanisms.name: Authority maps to believability but not only
mechanisms.paraphrase: Opinions are weighted by evidence of believability; management is subject to believability; yet merit cannot be the only factor in assigning authority (owners' vested interests count) and this must be explicit.

mechanisms.name: Hierarchy must get in sync downward
mechanisms.paraphrase: Those higher in the hierarchy must strive to get in sync with those lower about what makes sense; appeals go to a mutually agreed more believable arbiter.

mechanisms.name: Right to speak up, no silent dissent
mechanisms.paraphrase: Everyone has the right to understand what makes sense and no one may hold a critical opinion without voicing it; nothing is said about a person that would not be said to them.

mechanisms.name: Transparency enforces justice
mechanisms.paraphrase: Meetings are recorded; people can follow the discussion and the tape; those in charge must explain their thinking transparently; probing is transparent not private.

mechanisms.name: Principles as law
mechanisms.paraphrase: Principles cannot be ignored by mutual agreement; the same standards apply to everyone; Bridgewater moved from informal 'Articles of Confederation' to a written 'Constitution' with a judicial system.

mechanisms.name: Nobody above the system
mechanisms.paraphrase: No one may be more powerful than the system or so important as to be irreplaceable; governance directs and constrains leaders; beware fiefdoms.

mechanisms.name: Board, co-CEOs, independent assessors
mechanisms.paraphrase: A board selects and replaces CEOs and checks operation by principles, independent of CEO reporting lines (7-15 board members, 1-3 chairmen, 1-3 CEOs, 5-7 cabinet, ~50 succession pyramid); co-CEOs rather than one; assessors must have time, ability, and no conflict of interest; decision makers need information access and trustworthiness.

mechanisms.name: Right to complain is not right to decide
mechanisms.paraphrase: Do not confuse the right to complain, advise, or debate with the right to decide; consider the broader context a decision serves when challenging it.

mechanisms.name: Equal-weighted vote is advisory
mechanisms.paraphrase: Equal-weighted results are reported but not followed when they diverge from the believability-weighted result; random polling is rejected.

mechanisms.name: No anarchy, no mob rule
mechanisms.paraphrase: The right to argue is bounded by rules; crowds are emotional and seek control, so lynch mobs and mob rule are not permitted; once decided, everyone gets behind the decision.

mechanisms.name: Leader does not average opinions
mechanisms.paraphrase: A leader should neither ignore people nor blindly do what the average person wants, but surface disagreement and resolve it on the merits while logically assessing his own probability of being right.

mechanisms.name: Fairness of the system outranks outcomes
mechanisms.paraphrase: Care more that the decision-making system is fair and consistently well-managed than that you get your way.

mechanisms.name: Martial law only rarely
mechanisms.paraphrase: Suspend principles only in rare, declared, temporary circumstances; be wary of anyone arguing for suspension for the good of the organization.

mechanisms.name: Power must want the principles
mechanisms.paraphrase: If the people with power do not want to operate by principles the system fails, so power must be given to those who value it; no rulebook substitutes for a great partnership.

mechanisms.name: Transparency exceptions as expected-value calls
mechanisms.paraphrase: Exceptions to radical transparency are rare and decided as expected-value calculations on three narrow grounds (private/personal matters, harm to the organization's interests, low value versus high cost of sharing).

mechanisms.name: Independent problem-perceivers and auditors
mechanisms.paraphrase: Problem-perceivers and auditors have reporting lines outside the units they check so they can report without fear or capture.

mapping.dalio: Believability = probability a view is right, from track record plus reasoning quality (31, p94)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Per-forecaster credibility score from resolved forecasts under a proper scoring rule, plus a rated rationale-quality component

mapping.dalio: Believability tiers: repeated success AND good explanations when probed (31b, p95)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Two-axis reputation: resolved-call record and post-resolution rationale ratings; both high = top tier, one = middle, neither = novice

mapping.dalio: Baseball cards / believability matrix built from ratings, forced rankings, metrics, results (101b, p128)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Public per-forecaster scorecard: Brier/log score by domain, sample size, calibration curve, percentile rank

mapping.dalio: Believability-weighted voting (endnote 54, p192)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Aggregate forecast is a believability-weighted mean by domain rather than one-person-one-vote

mapping.dalio: Opinions should be costly, as in markets (p11, endnote 7)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Every submitted probability is scored on resolution; no unscored opinions in the credibility pool

mapping.dalio: Everyone may ask questions and hold theories; only believable people hold opinions (24b, 194)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Anyone may submit questions and scenarios unscored; only scored forecasts build credibility; tier is displayed beside each forecast

mapping.dalio: State confidence; suggestion vs conviction; the 51%-to-85% value (31b, 197c)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Forecasts must be numeric probabilities; calibration is tracked; the interface discourages default near-50% entries

mapping.dalio: Many decisions build a track record; luck cancels with sample size (p38, endnote 38)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Display n per forecaster; minimum resolved count before a credibility tier shows; confidence intervals on scores

mapping.dalio: Track record is level and slope, not wiggles (106d); level matters more than rate (207)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Rank on rolling score level with trend shown; don't reward recent improvement alone

mapping.dalio: Patterns not single events; five to ten observations (109a, 155)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: No tier change on one resolved call; tier moves require multiple resolutions

mapping.dalio: Issues log mandatory, rewarded when used, punished when skipped (19a, 144)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Mandatory post-mortem on every missed forecast; unresolved or unreviewed forecasts count against the forecaster

mapping.dalio: Accurate/inaccurate instead of blame/credit (14)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Scoring and review language is strictly accuracy; post-mortems are public, attributed and non-punitive in tone

mapping.dalio: Name names; no anonymous 'we' (15, 142, 150)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Persistent attributed identities (pseudonyms allowed) on every forecast; no anonymous entries in the scored pool

mapping.dalio: Record meetings and share; probing is transparent (6a, 99)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Immutable timestamped public ledger of forecasts, rationales and edits

mapping.dalio: No Monday-morning quarterbacking (159)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Score against information available at submission; locked timestamps; no retroactive edits

mapping.dalio: Mental map vs what happened; diagnostic question script (150)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Structured scenario template plus structured post-mortem fields: proximate cause, root cause, which step failed

mapping.dalio: Possibilities must carry probabilities (203)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Scenarios enter the scored pool only with a probability and a resolution criterion

mapping.dalio: 'By and large' true is true enough (204)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Resolution criteria define tolerance in advance; resolvers apply a by-and-large standard and log it

mapping.dalio: Triangulate with at least three believable people (195b)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Display the weighted aggregate of top-tier forecasters alongside the full-crowd aggregate

mapping.dalio: Debate is not a referendum; appeal to more-believable arbiters (28, 25, 36)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Resolution disputes go to a panel of high-believability forecasters, not a popular vote

mapping.dalio: Double-do: independent duplicates compared (184c)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Independent duplicate resolution by two resolvers; disagreement triggers review

mapping.dalio: Grader bias detected via average grades; forced rankings (144)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Monitor resolver and rationale-rater leniency; normalize ratings per rater

mapping.dalio: Auditors independent with undisclosed procedures (187a)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Resolvers independent of forecasters; audit sampling of resolutions not gameable

mapping.dalio: Metrics must not be gamed (144)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Proper scoring rules robust to question cherry-picking, e.g. coverage requirements and per-domain scores

mapping.dalio: Expected value, risk of ruin, 15+ uncorrelated bets (197)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Portfolio view of a forecaster's calls; bounded per-call scores; diversity across domains visible

mapping.dalio: Everything is a case study; identify principles violated (121, 160)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Post-mortems tag which forecasting heuristic failed, feeding a living manual of lessons

mapping.dalio: Believability = at least three successes on the thing in question plus explainable cause-effect reasoning (pp. 137, 261, 263)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Per-domain credibility that stays at zero until a minimum number of resolved forks (e.g., three) in that domain, and that counts only forecasts filed with a stated rationale; two sub-scores, resolved accuracy and reasoning quality rated after resolution by domain-credible peers.

mapping.dalio: Grading rule: neither criterion = not believable, one = somewhat, both = most (p. 263)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Three visible tiers per domain on a forecaster's card: unscored, track-record-only, track-record-plus-reasoning.

mapping.dalio: Believability is attribute-specific (p. 262)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Credibility computed per tag/domain, never as one global number; a fork's aggregation uses credibility in that fork's tags.

mapping.dalio: Track records accumulate and are open to scrutiny; self-report discounted (pp. 266, 294)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Append-only ledger of forecasts, updates, and resolutions; credibility derives only from resolved entries, never from profile claims.

mapping.dalio: Declare confidence up front; do not mistake possibilities for probabilities (pp. 264, 180)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Every forecast must carry a probability or distribution, scored with a proper scoring rule so stated confidence is what is scored.

mapping.dalio: Expected value; raising P(right) always valuable; knowing when not to bet (pp. 179-180)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Proper scoring rewards calibration at all levels; abstention is allowed and recorded without penalty; sample size shown next to every score.

mapping.dalio: Judge process plus outcomes over time; dots as at-bats (pp. 296, 299)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Scores shown with n and confidence intervals; per-forecaster trajectory charts; no leaderboard rank until a minimum number of resolved forks.

mapping.dalio: Equal-weighted and believability-weighted votes shown side by side; nubby questions flagged (pp. 261-262, 371)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Each open fork displays both the crowd mean and the credibility-weighted mean; forks where they diverge most are auto-flagged as high-information and routed to structured disagreement.

mapping.dalio: Auto-alert when you disagree with the believability-weighted majority; assume bias when several believable people disagree with you (pp. 371, 142)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: When a user's forecast is far from the credibility-weighted aggregate, the UI shows the gap and asks for reasoning; the divergence is logged so contrarian calls earn more when right and lose more when wrong.

mapping.dalio: Responsible Party may override the believability-weighted vote only at their peril (p. 267)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: A scenario owner's house call may deviate from the aggregate, but the deviation is itself a scored forecast attached to the owner's card.

mapping.dalio: Dot Collector (pp. 370-371)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: In-thread peer ratings on specific attributes of a contribution (evidence quality, calibration, synthesis) visible live and feeding the contributor's card; a per-fork poll with both aggregates.

mapping.dalio: Baseball Cards, People Profile, Combinator (pp. 371-372)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Public contributor card with per-domain scores, calibration curve, number of resolved forks, biggest hits and misses linked to the forks; a text summary; search for forecasters strong in a domain or complementary to a team; formula published and versioned.

mapping.dalio: Issue Log, mandatory, with severity and owner (p. 372)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Mandatory post-mortem on every resolved miss above a severity threshold: prediction, outcome, root cause (model, question, or resolution), responsible party; aggregated into error-type metrics by domain and question author.

mapping.dalio: Pain Button (p. 372)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Opt-in private miss journal attached to a resolved loss: log the reaction, reflect later with prompts, record the intended fix; the ledger later shows whether subsequent forecasts in that domain improved.

mapping.dalio: Dispute Resolver; escalate or vote; mutually agreed arbiter (pp. 373, 271, 268)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Resolution-dispute protocol: structured questions, a panel of domain-credible arbiters who did not forecast the fork, a deadline, a recorded verdict that stays attached to the fork.

mapping.dalio: Daily Update Tool (pp. 316, 373)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Periodic status feed on open scenarios (new evidence, probability changes, flagged issues) rolled into a dashboard; update frequency and responsiveness to evidence become open-mindedness metrics.

mapping.dalio: Contract Tool; implicit contracts are worthless; broken contract vs. unforeseen event (pp. 373, 322)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: A forecast is an explicit contract with resolution criteria, date, data source, and resolver named at filing; ambiguous forks are tagged as question-author failures, not forecaster failures.

mapping.dalio: Process Flow Diagram (p. 374)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Published pipeline diagram: submission, review, forecasting window, resolution, scoring, credibility update, with named roles and drill-down into each role's track record.

mapping.dalio: Policy and Procedures Manuals; policies extend principles; rare written exceptions (pp. 313, 374)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Versioned rulebook (scoring, resolution, disputes) with every change logged with its rationale; exceptions require a written proposal and a recorded decision.

mapping.dalio: Metrics cascade; four steps to good metrics (pp. 311, 374)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: System metrics (resolution latency, clean-resolution rate, dispute rate, aggregate calibration) cascading to domain metrics and individual cards.

mapping.dalio: Checklists; percent complete as a metric (pp. 296, 354)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Submission checklist (criteria, date, base rate, probability, rationale); a question-author's completeness rate is a metric.

mapping.dalio: Coach: situations linked to principles, with user feedback (p. 370)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Searchable casebook of past resolution rulings and edge cases that resolvers and forecasters consult; rulings link to the rule applied; users rate usefulness.

mapping.dalio: 5-Step Process (pp. 124-130)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Scenario lifecycle: question (goal), disagreement (problem), diagnosis of why forecasters differ, sharper forks (design), resolution and scoring (push through), iterated.

mapping.dalio: Diagnose the machine: outcome bad, who was responsible, capability or design (pp. 331-334)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: When the aggregate was badly wrong, a root-cause tag: forecaster pool, question design, or process; patterns by tag drive redesign.

mapping.dalio: Pain + Reflection = Progress (pp. 109, 252)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Post-mortems on misses are required for credibility to keep accruing; unreflected misses above a threshold freeze the card until the log is complete.

mapping.dalio: Thoughtful disagreement: teacher/student by believability, two-minute rule, argue vs. understand (pp. 137-138, 264-265)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Disagreement threads display each side's domain credibility, give each an uninterrupted opening statement, and tag replies as question or claim; lower-credibility participants are prompted to ask before asserting.

mapping.dalio: Stress-test theories from people without a track record (p. 264)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Newcomers can file forecasts immediately and earn credibility by resolution; included in the equal-weighted aggregate from day one and in the weighted aggregate once they have a record.

mapping.dalio: Open-mindedness cues (pp. 140-141)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Behavioral metrics on the card: questions-to-assertions ratio, update frequency after new evidence, how often a forecast moved after credible disagreement.

mapping.dalio: Principles to algorithms, tested on history; caution about opaque machine learning (pp. 181-187)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: All scoring and credibility code is public and backtestable on the ledger's own history; no opaque machine-learned weighting of forecasters.

mapping.dalio: Rater-bias controls, forced ranking, interviewer track records (pp. 312, 285)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Resolvers and peer raters get their own track records: strictness, dispute-overturn rate, ambiguity rate of questions they wrote.

mapping.dalio: Double-do; independent auditors; audit the auditors; sampling (pp. 344, 348, 298)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Two independent resolvers on high-stakes forks; random audits of resolutions by people outside the domain's resolver pool; audit outcomes published.

mapping.dalio: Nobody above the system; explicit decision rights; assessors without conflicts (pp. 359-361)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Administrators' and editors' calls are scored like everyone else's; resolvers cannot have forecast on the fork they resolve; vote weights in governance decisions are published.

mapping.dalio: No anarchy, no mob rule; equal-weighted vote is advisory (pp. 262, 272)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Equal-weighted crowd results are always displayed but never govern resolution or rule changes; rule changes follow the written process with credibility-weighted input.

mapping.dalio: Martial law rare and declared (p. 272)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Emergency overrides such as voiding a fork are rare, publicly declared, time-limited, and logged in the Issue Log.

mapping.dalio: Power must want the principles; no rulebook substitutes for partnership (pp. 273, 361)
mapping.open_ledger_equivalent: Governance is only as good as the key-holders; publish who they are and their own track records.

principles_2017.paraphrase: Be a hyperrealist: work from how things actually are, not how you wish they were.
An accurate understanding of reality is the necessary foundation of any good outcome.
Be radically open-minded and radically transparent; both accelerate learning through feedback.
Study how nature works and judge 'good' by what works for the whole, not by what feels good.
Improving through adaptation (evolving) is life's greatest accomplishment and its reward; individual incentives must align with the group's goals.
Apply nature's practical lessons: maximize your own evolution; no pain, no gain; strength comes from pushing limits.
Pain + Reflection = Progress: treat pain as a signal that there is something to learn, then reflect.
Weigh second- and third-order consequences, not only the immediate ones.
Own your outcomes regardless of circumstances.
Look at yourself and your situation as a machine from a higher level; modify the machine when outcomes miss goals.
Have clear goals; prioritize; do not confuse goals with desires.
Identify problems and refuse to tolerate them.
Diagnose problems down to their root causes before acting.
Design a plan that gets around the root causes.
Push the plan through to completion, using clear metrics to track progress.
Weaknesses do not matter if you find solutions; learn your own failure pattern and get help where you are weak.
Understand your own and others' mental maps and your degree of humility (knowledge vs. open-mindedness axes).
Recognize your two barriers: the ego barrier and the blind-spot barrier.
Practice radical open-mindedness: assume you may not know the best path; take in information first, then decide.
Value thoughtful disagreement as the way to find out which view is right.
Triangulate your view with believable people who are willing to disagree with you.
Learn the observable signs that distinguish closed-minded from open-minded behavior.
Learn how to become radically open-minded (habits, blind-spot lists, evidence, tools).
Knowing how you and others are wired is a source of power; measure attributes systematically (origin of Baseball Cards).
Meaningful work and meaningful relationships are biologically programmed needs, not luxuries.
Understand the brain's internal battles (conscious vs. subconscious, feeling vs. thinking, habit) and control them.
Find out what you and others are like using personality assessments.
Putting the right people in the right roles is the key to achieving any goal.
The biggest threat to good decisions is harmful emotion; decision making is two steps, learning then deciding.
Synthesize the situation at hand; choose carefully whom you ask; do not over-interpret a single data point.
Synthesize the situation through time: plot outcomes as dots, watch levels and rates of change, use 80/20.
Navigate levels of abstraction deliberately (above vs. below the line).
Logic, reason, and common sense are your best tools for synthesizing reality.
Make decisions as expected-value calculations.
Prioritize by weighing the value of more information against the cost of delaying a decision.
Simplify.
Use principles: treat each situation as another one of those, write down the decision criteria, refine them after outcomes.
Believability-weight your decision making.
Convert your principles into algorithms and let the computer decide alongside you.
Be cautious about trusting AI or machine learning without a deep understanding of the cause-effect logic.
There is nothing to fear from knowing the truth.
Have integrity and demand it: never say about someone what you would not say to them; loyalty to people cannot override truth.
Everyone has the right to understand what makes sense, and no one may hold a critical opinion without voicing it.
Be radically transparent; record almost everything; exceptions are rare and treated as expected-value calculations.
Meaningful relationships and meaningful work reinforce each other, especially under radical truth and transparency.
Be loyal to the common mission, not to anyone who is not operating consistently with it.
Be crystal clear on what the deal is (fairness vs. generosity; pay north of fair).
Organizational size threatens meaningful relationships.
Most people will pretend to act in your interest while acting in their own; watch conflicts of interest.
Treasure honorable, capable people who treat you well.
Mistakes are a natural part of the evolutionary process; fail well.
Do not worry about looking good; worry about achieving the goal; replace blame/credit with accurate/inaccurate.
Observe patterns of mistakes to see whether they are products of weaknesses.
Reflect when you feel pain; nobody can see themselves objectively; logging mistakes is mandatory.
Know which mistakes are acceptable and which are not, and do not permit the unacceptable ones.
Conflict is essential to great relationships; spend lavishly on getting in sync.
Know how to get in sync and disagree well; have clear paths from disagreement to decision (Dispute Resolver).
Be open-minded and assertive at the same time.
If it is your meeting, manage the conversation: purpose, level, two-minute rule, reach completion.
Great collaboration is like jazz; 1 + 1 = 3; three to five people beat twenty.
When you have alignment, cherish it.
If major differences, especially in values, cannot be reconciled, reconsider the relationship.
An effective idea meritocracy requires understanding the merit of each person's ideas.
Find the most believable people who disagree with you and try to understand their reasoning (criteria: at least three successes plus explainable cause-effect reasoning).
Know whether you are playing teacher, student, or peer in a given exchange.
Understand how people came by their opinions; capture track records systematically.
Disagree efficiently; believability weighting is a tool for, not a replacement of, decisions by Responsible Parties.
Everyone has the right and responsibility to try to make sense of important things, with the most relevant people involved.
Care more that the decision-making system is fair than that you get your way.
Principles cannot be ignored by mutual agreement; the same standards apply to everyone.
Do not confuse the right to complain, advise, or debate with the right to decide.
Do not leave important conflicts unresolved: escalate or vote.
Once a decision is made, everyone gets behind it even if they still disagree; no anarchy, no mob rule.
If the idea meritocracy conflicts with the organization's well-being, it will suffer; declare 'martial law' only rarely.
If the people with power do not want to operate by principles, the principled system will fail.
The most important decision is who you choose as Responsible Parties.
